html:
On 18 March 1938 President Lázaro Cárdenas of Mexico nationalised the oil industry, taking over the properties of American and British oil companies. The state company Pemex was founded that year.

The companies had refused to obey a ruling of the Mexican Supreme Court in favour of striking oil workers. Cárdenas announced the takeover on the radio. Huge crowds celebrated, and people of every class, including poor women, gave money, jewels and even chickens to help pay compensation.

Britain and Mexico broke off relations, and the companies boycotted Mexican oil, but the United States, wanting a friendly neighbour as war neared, accepted a settlement. Cárdenas also gave out more land than any earlier president, carrying out the promise of the revolution. The date is a national holiday in Mexico. Later nationalisations, from Iran to Venezuela, followed its example.
sum: On 18 March 1938 President Lázaro Cárdenas of Mexico nationalised the oil industry, taking over the properties of American and British oil companies. The state company Pemex was founded that year.
